clue.text: In exercise, exalt bishop — and thank the Lord!

indicators.note: 'In exercise' places the following words inside the letters for exercise

parts.note: PE is physical exercise, as in school PE lessons
to exalt is to raise up in praise
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A worshipper working out and glorifying a bishop gives thanks to God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' is the school subject, abbreviated, not the act of exercising.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of gratitude to God, used when something welcome finally happens.

clue.text: Drug dealer providing agriculturalist with abnormal growth, say?

indicators.note: 'say' signals that the phrase before it is to be spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a farmer with a cyst, run together and spoken quickly

explanation.surface: A drug pusher supplies a farmer who has some strange lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug dealer' suggests a criminal, but it is a perfectly legal chemist's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist legitimately dispenses medicines, so the playful description of one selling drugs is literally true.

clue.text: Those bits that are extra mature, snapped off externally

indicators.note: 'externally' means the rearranged letters go around the outside of the next piece
'off' suggests the word snapped has gone wrong, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to mature is to age

explanation.surface: Extra pieces of a well-aged item have broken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped off' looks like a break, but 'off' is the signal to rearrange, giving APPENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Attachments or limbs added onto a main body are surplus or supplementary parts.

clue.text: Challenging body

definitions.meaning: a slang word for a corpse

explanation.surface: A tough physique, or a demanding corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both hard or demanding and, as slang, a dead body.

clue.text: Lively man, children's entertainer?

parts.note: bouncy means lively and energetic
a castle (rook) is one of the men, or pieces, in chess

explanation.surface: An energetic fellow who keeps kids amused at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' looks like a person but is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable play structure that keeps youngsters amused at parties, cheekily called an entertainer.

clue.text: Dance has the talent, if you 16

indicators.note: 16-down is SEE DOUBLE, so the piece is written twice over

parts.note: if you can do something you have the ability for it

explanation.surface: A dancer is gifted, or so you'd think if you were seeing double.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 16-down tells you to double the piece: CAN twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively high-kicking French music-hall routine.

clue.text: Soldier shackling a young rogue, one solving others' problems?

indicators.note: 'shackling' means holding the following letters captive inside

parts.note: a soldier ant, so ANT

indicators.note: 'rogue' marks the letters of 'a young' as going astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier restrains a young villain, a sort of problem-solver for the community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' is the insect, not a person; 'rogue' reworks A YOUNG as GONYAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine columnist who answers readers' letters about personal troubles.

clue.text: See 24
Christmas prize giver, gutted

indicators.note: 'gutted' means the insides are removed, here the central letter

parts.note: the Nobel Foundation awards the Nobel prizes

explanation.surface: Someone handing out Christmas gifts is devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' removes the middle letter B from NOBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for the festive season, from French, heard in carols.

clue.text: A soft fabric binding linen at first, in sewing technique

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: 'binding' means holding the next letter wrapped inside

parts.note: piqué is a ribbed cotton fabric

indicators.note: 'at first' takes only the opening letter of linen

explanation.surface: Soft material enclosing some linen sounds like a description of needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' puts L, from 'linen at first', inside PIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative needlework where cut-out pieces of fabric are stitched onto a background.

clue.text: Pure beginner?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, having ..., so morally clean

explanation.surface: An innocent newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into NO VICE it means pure; whole, it means a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer or apprentice, and read as two words, someone free of wickedness.

clue.text: Submarine part defrauding tug?

parts.note: conning someone is swindling them
a tug is a boat that tows, so a tower

explanation.surface: Part of a submarine is involved in cheating a tugboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tug' is the vessel, read as something that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised structure on a submarine from which it is steered and its periscope raised.

clue.text: Plant ending in posy behind first of flowers picked by Eric Cantona, perhaps?

indicators.note: 'behind' places the final piece after the rest
'picked by' means the flower's letter is taken in by the following figure

parts.note: the French footballer played for Manchester United (Man U) and later became an actor

indicators.note: 'first of' takes the opening letter of flowers
'ending in' takes the last letter of posy

explanation.surface: A footballer chooses a flower for a bouquet, ending up with a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked by' puts F inside MAN U ACTOR, and 'behind' adds Y after.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a factory, and a plant is an industrial works.

clue.text: Banker close to golfer, one getting green fee on the house?

indicators.note: 'close to' takes the final letter of golfer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
vert is green in heraldry
rent is the payment made for living in a house

explanation.surface: A golfer on the green pays a fee to a banker hosting him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is something that has banks; the River Trent runs through the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, making it a cryptic 'banker'.

clue.text: Into bottom, bottom-pinching man with pretty woman aroused

indicators.note: 'Into bottom' means the rest goes inside the letters for bottom

parts.note: an end is the bottom of something

indicators.note: 'pinching' means gripping the next letters inside

parts.note: Richard Gere, the actor who starred in Pretty Woman
again, end means bottom

explanation.surface: A lecherous man and a pretty woman, getting excited.
explanation.walkthrough: Pretty Woman is the 1990 film co-starring Richard Gere; the hyphen makes him the one who is 'bottom-pinching'.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender feelings is to stir them up or provoke them.

clue.text: Men in leggings for riders

explanation.surface: Men wearing riding leggings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a word for fellows and for the leather leg coverings cowboys wear.

clue.text: Experience an illusion having date with a large drink

parts.note: to see someone is to date them
a double is a double measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Hallucinating after a date and a big drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' means go out with, not a calendar day.
explanation.definitionFit: Having blurred, doubled vision is a visual illusion, typically from drunkenness.

clue.text: See 21
Scottish author nevertheless Samoan at the end, by the way

indicators.note: 'by' means placed beside the rest

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
even so means nevertheless

indicators.note: 'at the end' takes the final letter of Samoan

explanation.surface: A Scottish writer who ended up in Samoa anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Louis Stevenson died in Samoa, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson, writer of Treasure Island, was born in Edinburgh.

clue.text: At that point, gathered's gathered

indicators.note: the second 'gathered' means collected in, so the first word holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A nonsensical line repeating that something was gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'gathered' signals the letters lying inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning in that place or at that moment.

clue.text: Book learned in Oxford, only covers erased

indicators.note: 'in' places the pieces inside the following letters
'only covers' takes just the outside letters of Oxford

parts.note: literate means learned or well-read

explanation.surface: A scholarly book from Oxford, rubbed out but for its covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' are the outside letters of the word, not a book's binding.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out completely is to erase all trace.

clue.text: Old commander in love with unit or wayward battalion, ultimately

parts.note: romance is love

indicators.note: 'wayward' signals the letters of 'unit or' straying into a new order
'ultimately' takes the last letter of battalion

explanation.surface: An ancient officer falls for a unit or an unruly battalion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' rearranges UNIT OR into NTURIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer in the ancient Roman army commanding about a hundred men.

clue.text: Goddess has life, if you 16

indicators.note: 16-down is SEE DOUBLE, so the piece is written twice over

parts.note: something that is exists, or has life

explanation.surface: A goddess lives, or so you'd think if you were seeing double.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 16-down tells you to double IS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian mother goddess of magic and fertility.

clue.text: Don't eat seconds in lard

indicators.note: 'in' puts the letter inside the next word

parts.note: lard is a fat

explanation.surface: Refusing second helpings cooked in lard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like extra helpings but is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without food deliberately, as in a religious observance.

clue.text: Fashion worn by companion in babyish sort of clothes, initially

indicators.note: 'in' places the letters inside the rearrangement
'sort of' says the letters of babyish are only a version of the word, so rearranged

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour

indicators.note: 'initially' takes the opening letter of clothes

explanation.surface: A style worn by someone's partner in childish clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' reworks BABYISH as SHABBYI; Companion of Honour is a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: An interior and clothing style using deliberately worn, distressed items.

clue.text: Promise clothes with identically matching tops for bikinis etc

indicators.note: 'clothes' means dresses around, so it wraps the following letters

parts.note: to swear is to promise

indicators.note: 'tops' takes the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A pledge that beach outfits will have matching tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here, meaning dresses or wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikinis are examples of costumes for the beach or pool.

clue.text: Model, a dolly?

definitions.meaning: someone who poses for a painter
in cricket, a dolly is an easy catch

explanation.surface: A doll-like fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket, a bat-and-ball game popular in Britain, calls an easy catch a dolly.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both a person posing for a portrait and, in cricket, an easy catch.

clue.text: Novel unread, it went

indicators.note: 'Novel' means new or fresh, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An unread novel, and it vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' is a euphemism for relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Going is a coy euphemism for passing water.
